detail.unboundHint: This instance has no bot account bound, so it never establishes a connection and never receives a message — it is not offline. A protocol endpoint that connects first registers itself as an unclaimed instance; claim it below. If nothing has connected yet, use "Bind account" below to type the account in directly.

unclaimedPanel.title_other: {{count}} protocol endpoints are connected but nobody has claimed them
unclaimedPanel.description: A protocol endpoint registers itself as an unclaimed instance when it connects. Until it is claimed it belongs to none of the instances you created — the one you created receives nothing.
unclaimedPanel.descriptionWithChannels_one: A protocol endpoint registers itself as an unclaimed instance when it connects, and messages and channels go to it. {{count}} channel currently sits under these unclaimed instances — if you cannot find your group in channel management, this is where it is.
unclaimedPanel.descriptionWithChannels_other: A protocol endpoint registers itself as an unclaimed instance when it connects, and messages and channels go to it. {{count}} channels currently sit under these unclaimed instances — if you cannot find your group in channel management, this is where they are.

claimDialog.title: Claim protocol endpoint
claimDialog.summary: Account {{account}} is currently registered under the auto-generated instance {{instanceKey}}, which owns {{count}} channels.
claimDialog.modeNewHint: Take over this protocol endpoint under a key of your choosing. Providing a new key creates an instance and moves the channels, messages and memories over; leaving it empty keeps the auto-generated key.
claimDialog.modeAdoptHint: Bind the account to an existing instance and move this endpoint's historical channels there. Use this when you created the instance first and the protocol endpoint registered a row of its own.
claimDialog.displayNameHelper: Leave empty to keep the name from registration
claimDialog.newInstanceKeyHelper: Leave empty to keep the auto-generated key; lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, max 32
claimDialog.instanceKeyInvalid: Instance keys allow lowercase letters, digits and underscores only, max 32 characters
claimDialog.noAdoptTargets: No eligible target under the same adapter: the target must not have an account of its own yet (one instance, one account).
claimDialog.confirmLabel: Type the unclaimed instance key to confirm
claimDialog.confirmMismatch: The instance key does not match
claimDialog.running: Moving channels and memories, do not close…

deleteDialog.title: Delete instance
deleteDialog.archiveDescription: Archiving stops the instance but keeps channels, messages and memories read-only for later handling.
deleteDialog.purgeDescription: Purging cascades to every channel, message and memory of this instance and cannot be undone.
deleteDialog.qbobAttached: This instance is connected to a QQ official bot in qbob. Deleting the instance does not delete that bot; it keeps running and retrying the connection. Disconnect it first on the Protocol tab of the instance.
deleteDialog.confirmLabel: Type the instance key to confirm
deleteDialog.confirmMismatch: The instance key does not match

messages.accountBound: Account bound, waiting for the protocol endpoint to connect
messages.accountUnbound: Account unbound; this instance will no longer send or receive messages

accountDialog.title: Bind a bot account
accountDialog.description: Inbound messages are routed to an instance by account. Enter the account the protocol endpoint logs in with (e.g. the QQ number) so this instance receives its messages. Leave it empty to unbind.
accountDialog.helper: One account can only be bound to one instance; if another instance already holds it you will be told to claim or unbind that one

onebotEndpoint.title: OneBot endpoint
onebotEndpoint.loadFailed: Failed to load the endpoint status

hints.snowluma: In the SnowLuma WebUI, open this account's OneBot configuration, find the reverse WebSocket node that connects to NA, turn on "Report self messages" and save. It takes effect immediately without dropping the connection.
hints.napcat: In the NapCat WebUI, open "Network Configuration", find the reverse WebSocket that connects to NA, turn on "Report self messages" and save.
hints.other: Turn on "Report self messages" (reportSelfMessage) in the endpoint's OneBot network configuration.
hints.suffix: Without it, messages sent by other programs on the same account never reach the chat history, and the AI cannot see them.

onebotEndpoint.undetermined: NA has not sent enough messages on this connection to tell yet. Send a few messages, then refresh.
onebotEndpoint.counts: On this connection: NA sent {{ownSends}} message(s), received {{echoes}} echo(es)

accessToken.title: Access token
accessToken.description: This instance's own OneBot access token. After rotating it the old token stops working immediately and connections to this instance that used it are dropped; rotating an exposed token makes the instance a trusted source again.
accessToken.copyFailed: Copy failed; select and copy it manually

confirm.title: Rotate access token
confirm.intro: The new token is generated on the server. Once you confirm, the old token stops working immediately and new handshakes no longer accept it; online connections to this instance that used it are dropped, and the endpoint must switch to the new token before it can reconnect.
confirm.napcat: Built-in NapCat: the network config is pushed again and the container is restarted, so the bot goes offline briefly. If the instance is disabled or the container is stopped, only the config is written and the container is not started.
confirm.remote: Remote endpoint: copy the new token into the endpoint's configuration afterwards; until then it cannot connect. If someone other than the platform runs this endpoint, handing them the new token still leaves the instance a trusted source for super-user chat commands, so think twice.
confirm.qbob: Built-in qbob: the new token is written back to qbob's endpoint configuration.

delivery.restarted: Configuration pushed and container restarted; the endpoint will reconnect with the new token.
delivery.config_written: The container is not running (or does not exist yet). The new configuration is written and takes effect when it starts.
delivery.rewired: The new token has been written back to qbob.
delivery.not_attached: The new token is in effect. No bot is attached in qbob yet; it will be used once one is.
delivery.manual: The new token is in effect. Copy it into the endpoint's configuration; until then the endpoint cannot connect.
delivery.failed: The new token is in effect, but it could not be delivered to the endpoint.

failedHint.napcat: Restart the container manually from the Protocol tab so the new configuration takes effect.
failedHint.qbob: Rewire qbob from the Protocol tab.
failedHint.remote: Change the token in the endpoint manually and reconnect.
failedHint.other: Restart the endpoint or rewire it manually.
